h1: Column and boom welding manipulators — 31.5 to 275.6″ lift and boom
intro: A column and boom (welding manipulator) holds the welding head — submerged arc, MIG or TIG — on a horizontal boom that travels up and down a column and in and out over the part, and feeds it along the seam at the welding speed: longitudinal seams of tanks and pipe, and, with turning rolls or a positioner turning the part beneath it, circumferential seams inside and outside. NovoTech's value-line manipulators, built in China, come in three sizes, all on this page, small to large: small manipulators with 31.5 to 78.7″ of lift and 39.4 to 78.7″ of boom travel, the column turned by hand; medium ones with 78.7 to 157.5″ of lift and 118.1 to 196.9″ of boom; and heavy ones with 196.9 to 275.6″ of lift and 236.2 to 315″ of boom, with motorized column rotation and carriage travel. Every model is available fixed, fixed with rotation or travelling with rotation, with arc auto-tracking, a TV monitor and flux recovery as options. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: What is a column and boom used for?
faq.a: Welding long and circumferential seams by machine: the boom puts the welding head over the seam and feeds it at the welding speed while the operator watches the arc. With the vessel on turning rolls the head stays still and the vessel turns for circumferential seams; with the boom feeding, it welds longitudinal seams — inside and outside of small tanks, longitudinal and transverse seams of large ones.

A fixed column suits a cell where the part comes to the machine. A fixed column with rotation swings the boom up to ±180° between two stations — weld one part while the next is loaded. A travelling column runs on rails along the work, for long vessels and several stations.

By the largest part: the lift has to put the head at the top of the largest vessel on its rolls, and the boom has to reach the far end of the longest seam — or inside the vessel for internal seams. Send us the diameters and lengths of your vessels and the welding process and we size the manipulator and the rolls under it.

Arc auto-tracking that keeps the head on the seam, a TV monitor for watching the arc from the control station, and a flux recovery and conveying system for submerged-arc welding. The welding power source and head are chosen for the process.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
